title: Comte d'Affry (The Hague) to Rouillé and Bernis, 1757-58, intercepted code letters (KHA Prins Willem V inv. 192, DECODE R1052-R1076)

documents.shelfmark: KHA Prins Willem V inv. 192; DECODE R1052-R1054, R1062-R1070, R1072-R1076

plaintext.source: Lyonet's contemporary clear decipherments of eight letters (R1052, R1053, R1062, R1063, R1065, R1066, R1069, R1075) are imaged on the DECODE records. The other ten letters have none on DECODE, but clerks' clear copies of all ten are in the digitised Fagel registers, Nationaal Archief 1.10.29 inv. 5186 (1757) and 5187 (1758), found by WAINUT (PR #65, 21 Oct 2026) after the reading; the Lyonet sets NA 1.01.50 inv. 221/223 are not digitised.

transcription.notes: One code: the former documents codeA (cipher_A.txt, Jan-Feb 1757, 5,011 groups) and codeB (cipher_B.txt, Apr 1757-Jan 1758, 3,512 groups) share their common values (NOTES "Codes"); cipher_U.txt holds both (8,523 groups, measured 14 Oct 2026). Uncertain digits marked ? in DECODE; first reading kept. Image re-transcriptions of R1064, R1067, R1072, R1074 in transcr/ replace the DECODE parse in measure_sense.py.

documents.shelfmark: KHA Prins Willem V inv. 192; DECODE R2067

system.summary: Numeric word-and-syllable nomenclator of about 1,200 groups (1-1199) with homophones, one code for d'Affry's letters Jan 1757 - Jan 1758.
system.notes: Groups separated by dots. A group-frequency cosine first split the letters into codes A and B; they share their common values, so A and B are one code (the split reflects homophone habits). R1071, in a different code C, was split off to affry1757c on 14 Oct 2026.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments by Lyonet (Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inv. 221, 223; not digitised); clerks' clear copies of all ten letters read here in the Fagel registers NA 1.10.29 inv. 5186/5187 (digitised; found by WAINUT 21 Oct 2026, after the reading, and not used for it); Dutch summaries with verbatim French sentences printed by Bussemaker, BMHG 27 (1906)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE records R1052-R1076 fetched with the session cookie: 65 images and 18 digit transcriptions.
DECODE 'solution on separate sheets' checked: no decipherment among the images.

De Leeuw thesis (2000) and Nationaal Archief 1.01.50 inventory: decipherments exist as inv. 221/223, not digitised; Bussemaker 1906 (DBNL) prints Dutch summaries with verbatim French sentences for 7 Jan, 1 Feb, 1 Apr, 19 Jul, 22 Jul 1757.
Group-frequency cosine between letters splits the series into three codes (A Jan-Feb 1757, B Apr 1757-Jan 1758, C R1071).
Numeric clustering of the 100 most frequent groups tested for a one-part (ordered) code: 23 adjacent pairs vs 15 random.
Bussemaker's verbatim 19 July 1757 passage placed in R1054 by the repeat 800 698 = 'des précautions' (13 groups apart vs 12 words); word-and-syllable code confirmed.
Bussemaker's 22 Jul and 1 Apr sentences: 'le danger de la religion' = 878 1117 813 1138 583 578 found in R1070 and R1054.
Coquelle, L'alliance franco-hollandaise (1904) on archive.org: verbatim quotes of d'Affry despatches, but of dates not in this set.
Coordinate-ascent LM solver (char 5-gram, corpus = clear parts of the letters + Coquelle) over group->string assignments from the crib seeds.
Local hard-EM aligner (cribalign.py) of the 19 Jul crib against R1054: second half aligned (des précautions, L.H.P., malgré, sagesse).
Re-examination of the images: the 'separate sheets' are imaged after all; Lyonet's clear decipherments found for R1052, R1053, R1062, R1063, R1065, R1066, R1069, R1075.
Clear copies transcribed from the images and aligned group by group with the cipher (EM aligner plus hand and sub-agent alignment) to rebuild the key.
Bussemaker's verbatim sentences (19 Jul, 22 Jul, 1 Apr) and Coquelle's quotation of the Gouvernante recur group for group in the key readings of R1054, R1070 and R1067.

Nine undeciphered letters (R1064, R1067, R1068, R1070, R1072, R1073, R1074, R1054, R1076) read with the voted key (651 groups) plus context inference by sub-agents, one letter each; DECODE digit slips (looped 8 read as 0, merged groups) corrected on the images.

Checked the 21 Sept measure (0.86): it counted any group with a key or inferred value, '?' included, regardless of sense, on cipher_U.txt, which keeps DECODE's 8-read-as-0 slips and drops every DECODE line opening with a paragraph tag (7 lines of R1064, 12 of R1065). Wrote measure_sense.py: valued group AND 9-group window scoring as French under lang fr-modern (per-char > -3.0); calibrated on the Lyonet letters' aligned sequences (0.876 pass).

R1072 (555 groups) and R1074 (537) re-transcribed from the images here; R1067 (1,481) re-transcribed and R1064 (1,243) checked line by line on the images by one image sub-agent at a time; R2067 hand transcription reformatted. Fixes: looped 8 read as 0, merged/dropped/added groups, one whole dropped line in R1064.

Open groups pooled over all letters (pool.py); 18 values forced by every occurrence added in key_X.tsv (1096 ir, 823 gra, 630 lui, 990 dit, 336 facil, 520 faire, 1102 Ecosse, 597 et, 303 la Gouvernante ...). 970, 869, 109/651, 731/708, 1191 and others left open: more than one word fits.

Re-measured with measure_sense.py: undeciphered letters 0.749 -> 0.824 of groups read as sense (R1072 0.661 -> 0.888, R1067 0.661 -> 0.791, R1074 0.702 -> 0.747, R1064 0.766 -> 0.808); all groups 0.823, 0.890 without R1071. 95% unreachable: R1071 (7.6% of groups) is in another code with no key.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 5587 tokens, 625 types, fr-modern order 4: reading -2.096 per letter; random keys -2.798 (z 13.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.127 (mean -2.136, z 4.3); annealer on the real text -2.126. Verdict: pass.

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1071 (code C, to Stainville) moved to affry1757c. Codes A and B merged into one document (one code, per the shared values). measure_sense.py rerun without R1071: 8,282/9,306 groups = 0.890.

WAINUT (PR #65): the Fagel registers NA 1.10.29 inv. 5186 (1757, 399 scans) and 5187 (1758, 225 scans) hold clerks' clear copies, in date order with number and addressee, of all ten letters without a Lyonet sheet on DECODE (R1054, R1064, R1067, R1068, R1070, R1072, R1073, R1074, R1076, R2067). WAINUT (PR #65) align_register.py: this folder's key (714 groups) against the register text of the ten letters, 4,333 of 5,554 keyed groups (0.780) take the register's word at that point; key values shuffled among groups (10 seeds) give 0.096-0.153 mean, 0.206 max per letter. R1076 and R1070 low (0.554, 0.593) because their first 157/139 groups get no register text; 0.92/0.91 on the aligned part.

WAINUT (PR #65): the registers settle 10 of the 16 open groups at grade H (e.g. 970 projets, 109 lundi, 651 mardi, 731 là dessus, 993 doit, 426 pouvoir) and 4 at M; contradict 64 key values at least twice (e.g. 675 vingt not deux, 1106 froid not succès, 762 occasion not égard, 1151 parce que not faire); give the register's word for 151 valueless groups; correct read/R1073.md in eleven places and R1068 (664 Vendredi; recipient Starhemberg, not d'Arenberg). Review of PR #65 (Bourdeau with Claude Opus 5.5): align_register.py re-run, every figure reproduced (4,333/5,554 = 0.780; per-letter table identical); R1068 decoded with the key gives 'm d a re m be r g' where the register (5186 181L) has 'Mr. Starrenberg', so the recipient on the page and read/R1068.md is corrected. The settled groups and key conflicts are not yet adopted: key_M and the measured 0.89 stand.

Every register candidate set against Lyonet's decipherments (align/R*.tsv, grade H): 7 dropped where Lyonet reads otherwise as often or more (16 le roi de Prusse, 94 peux, 605 inconvénient, 635 faut, 727 moi/mois 4:4, 895 devoir, 1193 utilité); 8 kept at M with one contrary Lyonet occurrence.

58 values folded into key_X.tsv / key_X.json: 21 open groups valued (970 projets, 109 lundi, 651 mardi, 731 là dessus, 774 résolution, 664 vendredi ...) and 37 values replaced (675 vingt, 1106 froid, 762 occasion, 1151 parce que, 992 er, 1027 le roi, 911 ns, 1039 et ...). measure_sense.py: undeciphered letters 4,797 -> 5,006 of 5,820 (0.824 -> 0.860); whole code 8,283 -> 8,492 of 9,306 (0.890 -> 0.913); Lyonet letters within a point. outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The code key (651 groups) was rebuilt by aligning Lyonet's contemporary clear decipherments of eight letters (R1052, R1053, R1062, R1063, R1065, R1066, R1069, R1075), imaged among the same DECODE records, with their ciphers; nine undeciphered letters of the same series were then read with it. Bussemaker's 1906 printed extracts served as a crib and check.
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure_sense.py (rerun 21 Oct 2026 after both passes of Fagel register values were folded into key_X.tsv): a group counts when it has a value (key_X.json, key_M.json, H/M rows of read/*_new.tsv) and its 9-group window scores as French (lang fr-modern, no spaces, per-char > -3.0); names in sense_names.tsv; transcr/R*.txt image re-transcriptions replace the DECODE parse. 8,761/9,306 groups: Lyonet-deciphered letters (3,486) counted read, the ten letters with no decipherment on DECODE 5,275/5,820 = 0.906. First pass only: 8,492 (0.913). 14 Oct, before the registers: 8,282 (0.890), 4,796/5,820 = 0.824. The same test passes 0.876 of the Lyonet letters' known-sense aligned text, so it under-counts. Revised 23 Oct 2026 (translation wave): R1054 and R1064 moved to decoded, not read (0.54, 0.57); 0.941 reduced by their share of the decryption words (2,198 of 11,625). Restored 23 Oct 2026 (r2q): R1054 and R1064 read from their Fagel register clear copies (scans checked, figures followed where they differ), so the measured 0.941 (8,761/9,306 groups) stands again. Rerun 27 Oct 2026 after R1054, R1068, R1070, R1073, R1076 were checked on the images (transcr/): 8,787/9,327 = 0.942.
outcome.notes: Read in part under the read bar: 0.89 of the code groups measured as sense; remaining open groups are codes several words fit and homophone clashes in the voted key. R1071, in another code, is a separate entry (affry1757c) since 14 Oct 2026. 21 Oct 2026: 0.941 of the groups (8,761/9,306) read as sense after 144 values from the Fagel register copies (NA 1.10.29 inv. 5186/5187), checked on the scans; 0.890 from the key alone, before the registers were known. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit (graded C): re-read; the keyed readings (read/R1054-R2067) build sentences with scattered bracketed codes, the first paragraph of R1054 being the worst; no letter relabelled, R1068 given reading_review B.

texts.label: R1054, 19 Jul 1757
texts.summary: The purpose of the Gouvernante's (Princess Anne's) journey to The Hague is not known. Some think she comes to push an augmentation of the land forces; her (pro-Orange / anti-French) party and even the ministers are starting to raise alarm; others say she wants a naval augmentation.

The contemporary clear copy is in the Fagel register, NA 1.10.29 inv. 5186 scans 248R-249L; WAINUT's Gemini transcription checked line by line against the NA IIIF scans (agrees word for word). 319/364 keyed groups stand at the register's word (0.876; shuffled 0.144). Reading follows the register in the clerk's spelling for the one cipher page on the record, and the figures where they give another word: 'à M. le Maréchal d'Estreés' (196 878 185; register 'au Cte.'; the DECODE parse had split 878^6 into 8 786), 'de sa communication' (10 = sa), and the page's last words 'que par le' (306 = par; register 'que je le voudrois'). Groups 101 and 760 (no value) are passed over as by the contemporary decipherer. Plain 1.0 (22/22), explicit 1.0. Log read/R1054_reread_log.md; parse corrections read/R1054_corrections.tsv.

texts.label: R1067, 1 Apr 1757, no. 161
texts.summary: D'Affry reports his interview with Pensionary Steyn on the King's orders (the demand for an answer on the passage of French troops by Maastricht/Namur): Steyn, embarrassed and under attack by enemies trying to bring him down, could not answer before the week-end. D'Affry then saw the Gouvernante (Anne of Hanover), gave her the King's declaration; she answered "must it be I who favour the means of doing harm to my father?" (George II); he asked her to use her credit to obtain the answer the King had a right to expect.

texts.label: R1073, 25 Jan 1757, no. 133
texts.summary: A rumour had spread that d'Affry had given the States General a memorial saying the King would regard an increase of the Republic's land forces as a breach of neutrality. The rumour was killed at once, but d'Affry saw the Grand Pensionary: the King did not and never meant to meddle in their internal affairs, but out of friendship would regret to see them commit to heavy expenses whose consequences the Republic should fear.

texts.label: R1076, 7 Jan 1757, no. 124
texts.summary: The Dutch, after the alarm over the convoy (four warships were to escort it, two were disabled by the storm), are relieved that it has arrived. D'Affry expects the naval armament of [n] ships to go through without any increase of the land forces, and says the argument will be pressed harder now that people see that the English will respect Dutch navigation only in proportion to the protection it has, so convoys through the Channel must be strongly escorted.
